name: Bumpcheck – PHP Upgrade Scanner
author: jolovicdev

sections.description:
Your host is moving your site to a newer PHP version. Bumpcheck tells you which plugins and themes would stop working, before the switch.

Pick a PHP version from 8.0 to 8.6 and run the scan. Each plugin and theme gets one of three results:

  • Breaks: it calls something that the chosen PHP version removed. The page shows the file, the line and what to use instead.
  • Works, uses deprecated code: it runs, but PHP will log deprecation notices.
  • Ready: nothing found.

What makes it different

  • It reads the files on your server. Premium plugins, custom plugins and your own theme are checked like everything else.
  • Nothing leaves your site. No account, no outside service, no data sent.
  • It covers PHP 8.0, 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 8.5 and 8.6.
  • It does not time out. The scan runs in short steps. In our test, 21,000 files took 13 seconds.
  • It knows about old fallback code. Many plugins keep a branch for ancient PHP versions that never runs on your site. Those lines are listed apart and do not count against the plugin.

What it checks

Removed and deprecated functions, constants and INI settings. Array offsets with curly braces. The (unset) and (real) casts. Constructors named after their class. "${var}" in strings. Missing return types on ArrayAccess, Iterator, Countable and JsonSerializable methods. Serializable without __serialize(). Parameters that are nullable only through a null default. Required parameters after optional ones. get_class() without an argument. A third argument to define(). Deprecated mb_convert_encoding() encodings.

What it cannot check

The scan reads code and does not run it. Problems that depend on values at run time are out of reach, for example passing null to a function that needs a string, or properties created on the fly (deprecated in PHP 8.2). A clean result means nothing known was found. Test on a staging copy before you switch a busy site.

Bumpcheck Pro

A separate add-on adds a weekly or daily scan with the result by email, CSV and JSON export, and a WP-CLI command. Details and price: getbumpcheck.com.
sections.faq:
Does it change anything on my site?

No. It reads files and stores the result of the last scan. Deleting the plugin removes that result.

Does it check WordPress itself?

No. WordPress core supports the PHP versions listed on wordpress.org. Bumpcheck checks what you added: plugins, must-use plugins and themes.

A plugin shows “already true on my PHP version”. What does that mean?

The code uses something that was removed in a PHP version you already run. If that code ran, it would fail today. It is almost always an old fallback branch, so it does not count as a result of the upgrade.

Is a “Ready” result a guarantee?

No. See “What it cannot check”.
